name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: We should integrate Kaedim's AI-powered 3D asset production into our workflow to boost link coverage. This decision allows us to leverage Kaedim's advanced technology to generate high-quality 3D assets, which will help increase link coverage at a faster rate. By doing so, we're accepting the trade-off of relying on an external tool, which may introduce some dependency risks, but the potential benefits to our link coverage goal outweigh these risks. This integration will also enable us to focus on other aspects of the project, such as refining our model thresholds, to further improve overall quality.

name: Scriv
text: Kaedim’s AI tools won’t fix broken link coverage—they mask the real problem: our audit logic still trusts the model to self-report. The risk? We trade one gap (manual checks) for another (hidden failures in Kaedim’s pipeline). Better alternative: audit Kaedim’s output against a *static* reference set first, then measure link coverage. Settle it by running a blind test—feed Kaedim’s assets into our existing validator and see if the numbers hold.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt Gluestack UI MCP Server to cover UI link testing. It plugs directly into our test harness, giving us immediate coverage of UI components without rewriting audits. The trade-off is vendor lock-in to Gluestack’s MCP protocol, but it’s pre-approved and faster than building a custom solution.

name: Sift
text: Gluestack’s MCP Server outsources the black-box problem to another vendor—we still can’t audit its internal logic, just its outputs. The real risk is trading one untestable system (our model) for another (Gluestack’s pipeline), with no way to verify correctness. Settle this by demanding open-source audits of Gluestack’s MCP layer or building a parallel static reference checker to validate its outputs.

name: Scope
text: Adopt Gluestack UI MCP Server to cover UI link testing. It plugs directly into our test harness, giving us immediate coverage of UI components without rewriting audits. The trade-off is vendor lock-in to Gluestack’s MCP protocol, but it’s pre-approved and faster than building a custom solution.

name: Scriv
text: The real risk with adopting Gluestack UI MCP Server is that we're exchanging one potential point of failure for another, without addressing the underlying issue of auditability. A better alternative would be to develop a custom, open-source solution that allows us to maintain control over the entire testing pipeline. This argument would be settled by conducting a thorough cost-benefit analysis of developing a custom solution versus relying on a vendor-locked, black-box system like Gluestack's MCP Server.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Split effort 50% Kaedim (audit transcripts + product pages against static references) and 50% Glue (build custom open-source MCP server for UI link testing).

Result must deliver: 100% link coverage with auditable outputs, no hidden failures.
Owners: Kaedim team (transcripts), Glue team (UI MCP server).
